1.note: Literally "the married paths became virgins": roads that were once trodden became untrodden. The Hebrew rhymes בְּעוּלוֹת (married) with בְּתוּלוֹת (virgins).

2.note: Job 29:6 "when I washed my steps in butter", a figure of prosperity. The rhyme word חֵמָה (butter) plays on חֵמָה (fury) in the line before.

3.note: שִׁנֵּיהֶם (their teeth) rhymes with and puns on שְׁנֵיהֶם (the two of them) two lines before.

4.note: Job 41:14 "in his neck lodges strength" and Job 39:19 "have you clothed his neck with a mane (רַעְמָה)?", said of the war horse. רַעְמָה can also be heard as "thunder", and the next line uses Raamah as a name of a people (Gen 10:7).

5.note: Ps 94:17 "my soul would soon have dwelt in silence (דּוּמָה)". The word repeats the name Dumah at the end of the line before.

6.note: נָשַׁק "kiss" sounds like נֶשֶׁק "weapon", and the "mouth of the sword" (פִּי חֶרֶב) is its edge.

7.note: Read as "those who join battle". The word also means "innards" (קְרָבַיִם), so the rebuke may wage war "within the inward parts". It plays on קְרָבוֹת (battles).

8.note: The blade is fire in its effect and water in its sheen; Arabic poetry often calls a polished sword "water". Compare line 88, where the sword "thirsts for water".

9.note: Uncertain. Perhaps: whoever sees how I begin a fight will share the end I bring on my foes, that is, his death.

10.note: הֲדוֹם is a footstool; the earth is God's footstool (Isa 66:1). So: heaven and earth.

11.he: וְהָאֵמִים לְפָנִים יָשְׁבוּ בָהּ / וְהִיא מָעוֹן לְכָל-פַּחַד וְאֵימִים
11.note: Deut 2:10 "the Emim dwelt in it formerly", said there of the land of Moab, here of the sword. The rhyme word אֵימִים (terrors) repeats the name Emim.

12.note: Gen 37:7 "we were binding sheaves" (מְאַלְּמִים אֲלֻמִּים), Joseph's dream. The verb and its noun are of the same root.

13.note: A pun: כְּפִירִים "young lions" and כְּפָרִים "villages" differ only in vowels.

14.note: Ps 68:14 "between the sheepfolds" (or "hearths"); a word of uncertain meaning. Here perhaps "between the two battle lines".

15.note: Gen 38:14, a place name (Petaḥ Enaim). Literally "at the opening of the eyes", that is, in full view of each other.

16.note: 1 Sam 17:4, of Goliath: "the man between the two camps", the champion who stands between the armies and calls out to them. The Hebrew plays on בֵּינֵיהֶם (between them) earlier in the line.

17.note: Literally "the burning hearths of the house". Like the fallen "mountains" and "pillars" before it, probably a figure for the great men who died.
